errorCodes.meaning: The caller is not permitted to write memory in the named context.
The `expectedVersion` precondition failed. The details carry the maintainer's current version and value, so the caller can resolve without a re-read.
The value exceeds the VTA's documented per-item cap. The details carry both the cap and the actual size.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

MemoryExpectedVersion.description: Optimistic-concurrency precondition on a write. A positive value requires that the item's current `version` equals it exactly. Zero means "create only" — the write applies only if no LIVE item exists at the key. A tombstone is not a live item, so `expectedVersion: 0` succeeds over one; the created item takes the context's next counter value, which is necessarily greater than the tombstone's.
MemoryExpectedVersion.title: MemoryExpectedVersion

MemoryKey.description: Agent-chosen identifier for an item within a context. Opaque to the maintainer: it MUST NOT be parsed, normalized, or case-folded, and prefix matching in `vta/memory/list` is a byte-prefix comparison over the UTF-8 encoding. Agents SHOULD use `/`-delimited hierarchical keys (`contact/billing`, `preference/timezone`) so that `prefix` can address a family of items, but the delimiter is a convention between an agent and itself. A key is content as well as an address: a key naming a person, a condition or a dispute discloses something to anyone who can list the context, even without its value.
MemoryKey.title: MemoryKey

MemoryValue.description: The remembered text: a fact, a summary, a preference. Opaque to the maintainer, which stores it as given and never interprets, rewrites or summarises it. The maintainer enforces a documented per-item cap on its size (see `vta/memory/put`).
MemoryValue.title: MemoryValue

MemoryVersion.description: A value of the context's monotonic write counter (see this schema's description). Server-assigned; a producer never chooses one.
MemoryVersion.title: MemoryVersion

Response.description: Success response to vta/memory/put. Type https://trusttasks.org/spec/vta/memory/put/0.2#response. A failed precondition is not a success: it is a trust-task-error carrying vta/memory/put:versionConflict, whose details carry the maintainer's current version and value.

valueBytes.description: Size of the stored value in bytes as the maintainer measured it against its per-item cap.

version.description: The version this write took. Supply it as `expectedVersion` on the next write to chain conditional updates without an intervening read.

wasCreated.description: True when no live item existed at the key beforehand — including when the key held a tombstone, since a tombstone is not a live item.

Response.title: VTA Memory Put — response payload

schema.description: Store one memory item at its `(contextId, key)` address. `expectedVersion` makes the write conditional: a positive value requires the item to be at exactly that version, and zero requires that no live item exists.

contextId.description: The VTA context the item is scoped to; the isolation boundary.

expectedVersion.description: Optional precondition. Omit for a last-writer-wins upsert, as in 0.1. Supply the version a prior read returned to make the write conditional; supply 0 to create only.

schema.title: VTA Memory Put — payload
